summary.description: A documentation architect and maintainer for source-grounded documentation.

avoid: Application or source changes, invented behavior, marketing copy, or edits to source comments or docstrings.
An obvious isolated one-line update that the current implementer can make without research or cross-document reconciliation.
delegateWhen: Behavior, setup, configuration, commands, or public interfaces changed and documentation surfaces may now be stale.
Documentation structure, navigation, duplication, broken links, onboarding, or ownership needs coherent documentation-only changes.
A source-grounded reference, migration guide, or cross-document reconciliation is needed.
routing.lane: Use when documentation needs coherent, source-grounded maintenance.

summary.description: A standalone, read-only maintenance auditor for repository maintainability.

avoid: Feature implementation, a concrete bug fix, security or performance review, or executing cleanup.
Formatting, stylistic preference, naming bikeshedding, or speculative abstraction without demonstrated maintenance cost.
The exact small cleanup is already known and needs an implementer rather than an audit.
delegateWhen: Repository change cost is rising due to duplication, dead paths, tangled ownership, oversized or mixed-responsibility modules, or stale scaffolding.
A substantial refactor, migration, or release needs a read-only maintainability audit that prioritizes worthwhile cleanup.
routing.lane: Use when the repository is getting harder to change.

summary.description: A standalone, read-only security reviewer for architecture and code risk.

avoid: Implementation, generic code quality, maintainability, or performance work without a security boundary.
The declared deployment model makes the alleged threat inapplicable and no credible attacker path remains.
The request requires live probing, pentesting, or a security guarantee.
delegateWhen: A change crosses a trust boundary or handles authorization, sessions, secrets, untrusted input, or files.
A change handles external requests, command execution, payments, or sensitive state.
A concrete change or architecture needs threat modeling, pre-release security review, or validation of a suspected vulnerability.
The exploitability or impact of a security finding is unclear and needs code-grounded triage.
routing.lane: Use when a change crosses a meaningful trust boundary.

summary.description: A read-only code-review arbiter for completed implementation work, correctness, architecture, contracts, and merge readiness.

avoid: The task is implementation, documentation, or a narrowly specialized audit better handled by another reviewer.
There is no concrete completed change, diff, or implementation scope to inspect.
delegateWhen: A completed implementation step or pull request needs review for correctness, architecture, contracts, testing, or significant risks.
A substantial change needs a second opinion against its plan, requirements, repository conventions, or intended behavior.
Merge readiness is uncertain because the change may contain cross-cutting correctness or design problems.
routing.lane: Use after meaningful implementation work needs an evidence-backed merge-readiness review.

summary.description: A source-grounded documentation specialist for durable project docs, changelogs, architecture, migrations, and other descriptive artifacts.

additionalInstructions: Never use Chronicler for session handoffs, conversation-state synthesis, context compaction, or similar parent-context work.
Never use Chronicler to implement outputs of /reflect or other harness self-improvement workflows.
avoid: The output depends materially on parent-session conversation, orchestration state, decisions, attempted approaches, or other non-reconstructable context.
The task creates or modifies behavior-defining harness artifacts such as skills, agent prompts, commands, routing rules, or harness configuration.
The task is a reflection or self-improvement workflow whose resulting skills, agents, commands, or configuration must remain Orchestrator-owned.
The task is primarily functional implementation, deep code review, or broad product strategy rather than descriptive documentation.
delegateWhen: A durable README, API reference, changelog, release note, architecture document, migration guide, or technical guide needs writing or revision.
Implementation or configuration changed and descriptive documentation needs source-grounded reconciliation.
Technical documentation needs evidence from repository reality, current library docs, or narrow external code references.
routing.lane: Use for durable, descriptive project documentation whose facts are reconstructable from stable evidence.

summary.description: A read-only error-path hunter for swallowed failures, misleading fallbacks, weak diagnostics, and hidden retry exhaustion.

avoid: The task is generic code review with no meaningful error-handling, retry, fallback, or failure-propagation surface.
The task is to implement the fixes rather than audit existing behavior.
delegateWhen: A change adds or modifies catch blocks, retries, fallback logic, error conversion, recovery, or default-on-failure behavior.
A suspected failure may be swallowed, hidden, downgraded, or surfaced without enough information to act.
A completed change needs focused review of user-visible or operator-visible failure paths.
routing.lane: Use to audit error handling, fallback behavior, retries, and failure propagation.

summary.description: A read-only test-sufficiency specialist focused on behavioral coverage, regression risk, and high-value test gaps.

avoid: The task is general code review, implementation, or writing tests rather than evaluating test sufficiency.
The change is trivial and its test implications are already obvious from existing coverage.
delegateWhen: A pull request or completed change needs its test coverage evaluated for realistic regression risk.
New or modified behavior needs verification that important success, failure, boundary, or integration paths are tested.
Existing tests need review for behavioral value, resilience, and meaningful assertions rather than line coverage.
routing.lane: Use to assess whether a completed code change has sufficient behavioral tests.
